videos.desc:
By 1780, the American Revolution was being lost in the South. Then, on a cold January morning, a crippled frontier
wagon driver wiped out Britain's most feared legion in less than an hour.
In this video we break down Daniel Morgan's three greatest tactical moves: the riflemen who shot down Burgoyne's
officers at Saratoga, the trap at Cowpens that destroyed Banastre Tarleton's command, and the blueprint he left
Nathanael Greene before Guilford Courthouse, the road that led Cornwallis to Yorktown.

videos.title: 2 Para's Top 3 Legendary Tactical Moves | The Bluff That Won the Falklands' First Land Battle
videos.desc:
2 Para’s legendary tactical moves at Goose Green defined the Falklands War. See how they took 961 prisoners against the odds.

On May 27, 1982, British paratroopers initiated a daring assault on the garrison. Despite being heavily outnumbered and facing a dug-in enemy that knew they were coming, the battalion executed a series of maneuvers that secured a decisive victory. This analysis covers the leadership of Major Chris Keeble and the risks taken during the engagement in the Falklands War.

We examine the night assault from Camilla Creek House, the grueling fight for Darwin Hill and Boca Hou

videos.title: George Thomas's Top 3 Legendary Tactical Moves | The Man Who Saved the Union Army
videos.desc:
George H. Thomas held the line at Chickamauga after a third of the Union army ran from the field. Fifteen months later, days before Ulysses Grant could relieve him of command, he broke John Bell Hood's army at Nashville.

He was a Virginian from the same state as Robert E. Lee, and when Virginia left the Union in 1861 he stayed loyal to his oath. His own sisters turned his portrait to the wall and never spoke to him again. On 20 September 1863, one confusing order opened a quarter-mile gap in the Union line at Chickamauga, Longstreet's column poured through it, and the army commander rode back
